events.continuity_hook: Finalizes the Carolina controls-workshop trip after the return window and hotel-location trade-off are settled.
events.interaction_goal: Book the flights, rental car, hotel, room request, seat selections, and compact agenda for the workshop, dinner, plant walk-through, and procurement meeting.
events.scenario_brief: The Carolina utility confirms the Thursday procurement meeting should end near noon but could slip, so Jonah rules out the tight midafternoon return and chooses an early-evening flight. He books the Monday afternoon Bay Area-to-Charlotte nonstop over cheaper one-stop options, keeps a compact rental car, and chooses the airport-area hotel with solid guest feedback, parking, and easier plant access rather than the uptown property. The reservation should include a coffee maker and mini-fridge request, and window seats should be selected where available.

events.continuity_hook: Adds a final practical timing check to the already booked Carolina trip once the utility visitor details arrive.
events.interaction_goal: Update the concise Carolina itinerary with the revised badge, gate, dinner, hotel, rental-car, and airport timing while leaving reservations unchanged.
events.scenario_brief: The Carolina utility sends the visitor packet after booking, moving the Wednesday plant walk-through to a west gate check-in and adding a badge pickup step before the Tuesday workshop. Jonah does not want to revisit the booked flights, rental car, or airport-area hotel; he only needs the arrival-night drive plan, Tuesday distributor-dinner parking, Wednesday gate buffer, Thursday checkout timing, and airport return timing tightened around the new instructions.

events.continuity_hook: Starts a new food-and-beverage plant site visit after the Carolina trip logistics are settled.
events.interaction_goal: Create a flight, rental-car, and hotel shortlist that protects the early Wednesday plant access window while leaving room for a possible Thursday extension.
events.scenario_brief: A beverage bottling plant in the Inland Empire asks Jonah to review a membrane retrofit after a pressure-spike issue, with a Tuesday afternoon instrumentation review and a Wednesday 6:00 a.m. sanitation/CIP observation. He needs Monday Bay Area-to-Ontario or Burbank flight options that leave enough time for a rental-car pickup and prep that evening, with clean routing more important than carrier. Hotels should compare an Ontario airport option against Rancho Cucamonga or Fontana properties closer to the plant and evening meals. The unresolved items are whether a Thursday engineering closeout will be added and whether the spare sensor kit reaches the plant before Tuesday.

events.continuity_hook: Moves the Inland Empire retrofit trip from comparison to booking after the equipment and closeout schedule are clarified.
events.interaction_goal: Finalize the flights, rental car, hotel reservation, room request, seat choices, and two-day plant agenda.
events.scenario_brief: The plant confirms the spare sensor kit has arrived and drops the Thursday engineering closeout, but adds a Wednesday afternoon controls debrief before Jonah can leave. He chooses the Monday afternoon Oakland-to-Ontario nonstop and a Wednesday evening return because it is more predictable than the lower-cost connecting alternatives, books a compact rental car, and selects the Rancho Cucamonga hotel with strong guest feedback, parking, and nearby restaurants. The room note should request a coffee maker and mini-fridge, with window seats selected where available.

events.continuity_hook: Starts a lighter personal travel episode after the Inland Empire client visit is booked.
events.interaction_goal: Build a practical flight, rental-car, and hotel shortlist for the long weekend, centered on schedule comfort, hotel quality, and dinner access rather than work logistics.
events.scenario_brief: Jonah and his spouse are considering a Santa Fe long weekend after several work trips, using a Friday-to-Monday window with two tickets and a rental car from Albuquerque. His spouse may be able to leave after lunch Friday but has not confirmed, so he wants to compare midafternoon and early-evening Bay Area departures with at most one reasonable connection. Hotels should focus on well-rated properties near the Plaza with walkable dinner options and flexible cancellation; work-trip room basics are less important here. The open item is whether the Friday departure can be early enough to reach Santa Fe before a late dinner.

events.continuity_hook: Finalizes the Santa Fe long-weekend plan once the Friday departure constraint is resolved.
events.interaction_goal: Book the weekend flights, hotel, rental car, and seats, then summarize the Friday arrival and Monday return timing.
events.scenario_brief: Jonah’s spouse confirms she can leave work by noon Friday, making the midafternoon outbound workable. He picks the Bay Area-to-Albuquerque itinerary with one comfortable connection that arrives early enough for the drive to Santa Fe, holds a Monday afternoon return, reserves a midsize rental car, and chooses the higher-rated Plaza-area hotel with easy restaurant access. Seat selection should keep them together, with a window seat where it fits, and the only remaining optional item is whether to add a dinner reservation for the first night.
